title: Resolve manifest merge conflict causing on-prem operator reconcile failures and deliver live hotpatch
creator: Miguel Santos
description:
Summary:
A subset of customers running the on-prem Operator observed reconcile failures after an operator-anchored Helm upgrade. The operator entered crashloop/reconcile stalls due to a manifest-level merge conflict introduced by a change in our Helm overlay semantics: array fields in tenant overrides were being merged instead of replaced, producing duplicated annotation keys and an invalid finalizer set that the mutating webhook rejected. The result: stuck upgrades, controller restart loops, and tenant-level config drift (annotations/finalizers inconsistent with cluster expectations).

Root cause (investigation notes):
- Recent operator upgrade (onprem-operator-2026.03 alpha) introduced an overlay merge helper that attempts deep-merge of arrays to avoid losing user overrides.
- For some tenant CRs we saw duplicated annotation entries (same annotation key serialized twice in the manifest list) and conflicting finalizer arrays (order/dup entries), which triggers our mutatingwebhook/validation logic to reject server-side apply attempts when the operator tries to reconcile.
- The operator's reconcile loop retries fast and eventually exceeds kube-apiserver rate limits, leaving controllers in crashloop or stuck reconcile state.
- Helm post-upgrade hooks that attempted remediation ran but relied on non-transactional apply semantics and caused partial state writes, increasing drift.

Customer impact:
- High: several on-prem customers reported tenant downtime or inability to complete upgrades. Escalations opened with Support and SEs.

Goals for this ticket:
1) Provide a safe live hotpatch that patches operator to detect and sanitize duplicate annotations/finalizers before apply (stop-gap).
2) Deliver a durable operator fix that changes overlay semantics back to safe replace-for-arrays and adds preflight validation + transactional reconcile path.
3) Author and ship a runbook for manual remediation for affected tenants (audit, sanitize, resume).
4) Communicate with impacted customers and coordinate rolling patch/upgrade windows.

Proposed technical approach (phased):
Phase 0 — Emergency live hotpatch (target within 24–48h):
- Implement a small change in operator reconcile: pre-apply sanitizer that normalizes annotation keys (de-duplicate by last-wins) and canonicalizes finalizer lists (stable order, remove duplicates).
- Add a guard: if an apply fails due to admission/validation, operator will backoff to 1m and mark tenant as "upgrade-pending-manual-sanitize" and emit a clear event + metric (tenant.sanitize_required=1).
- Build a Helm chart patch release for customers to opt into as a hotpatch: operator image X (hotfix build) + small preflight job.
- Smoke test against a reconstructed tenant in staging that reproduces the failure (script included in links).

Phase 1 — Durable fix (safe runtime change in next minor release):
- Revert array deep-merge for Helm overlay step: implement replace semantics for top-level arrays used by our CRs (annotations, finalizers, volumes list, etc.) with opt-in deep-merge per-schema when safe.
- Switch operator apply path to server-side apply with fieldManager and use last-applied metadata where appropriate so partial writes are prevented.
- Add preflight validation step that runs a dry-run server-side apply to detect admission rejections and expose human-friendly diagnostics in operator status.

Phase 2 — Postmortem, tests, and rollout controls:
- Add unit/integration tests that simulate array merge cases and ensure sanitizer corrects them.
- Add e2e upgrade test to our CI that performs a canary with 5 tenants and validates idempotent upgrade.
- Dashboarding: add Grafana panels for reconciliation error rate, apply rejection reasons, and count of tenants flagged sanitize_required.

Rollout & rollback plan:
- Canary (hosts): ship hotpatch image to 2 internal staging clusters, verify for 24h.
- Customer canary: offer hotpatch to two impacted customers with SE support window.
- Ramp to auto-upgrade pool with 10% of tenants, monitor metrics for 48h.
- Full rollout after metrics stable for 72h.
- Rollback: publish Helm rollback chart and a quick job to revert operator image and re-run previous reconciliation semantics.

Manual remediation runbook (attached in links):
- Identify affected tenant namespace from support ticket (use dashboard query listed below).
- Snapshot tenant CR (kubectl get -o yaml), create temp copy, sanitize annotations/finalizers using provided sanitize script (links), apply via kubectl apply --server-side=false to avoid validating webhook blocking when using hotpatch path.
- Reconcile: kubectl annotate tenant redwood/upgrade-resume=true to trigger operator resume hook.

Telemetry & alerts:
- New metric: operator.sanitize_required{tenant} incremented when apply fails with validation error.
- Alert: Pager if reconcile_errors_total spikes > 10/min across control-plane for 15m or if >3 customer escalations in 2h.

Security considerations:
- Sanitizer runs only on operator-managed fields (annotations/finalizers); does not touch customer config.
- Security review requested for server-side apply changes in Phase 1 (see security_review_required).

Acceptance criteria:
- Hotpatch image released and validated in staging with the reproduce script.
- One affected customer validated that their upgrade resumed after hotpatch and data integrity intact.
- Durable code change merged and gated by e2e tests for array overlay cases.
- Runbook published to Confluence and shared with Support/SE teams.

Notes & follow-ups:
- Find exact tenants that saw failures and consolidate logs (see links to Kibana/Grafana).
- Coordinate with Platform on operator image promotion and Dedicated/private release windows.
- Postmortem to be authored once fix is stable; include timeline and RCA details.

2026-03-07 — PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/4821 — small pre-apply sanitizer + metric emissions. Requesting urgent review from runtime and infra leads.

2026-03-09 — Review: Security reviewed initial sanitizer logic — no secret exposure, but Phase 1 server-side apply changes flagged for formal security review. QA requested additional test where webhook denies partial writes.
2026-03-11 — QA: Hotpatch deployed to staging clusters (staging-1, staging-2). Reproduction script rerun; manifests now sanitize and reconcile completes. Added smoke test to upgrade-e2e pipeline.

2026-03-12 — Customer rollout: Hotpatch scheduled for customer A (maintenance window 2026-03-14 03:00 UTC). SEs notified and runbook provided. Monitoring dashboard created: dashboards/upgrade-reconcile-errors (Grafana).
2026-03-13 — Current: Waiting on sign-off from Product and Platform for canary ramp. Draft postmortem outline created (confluence link below).
